claims: C1: The best-intentions biases are subtle defaults only.
C2: These defaults must never override explicit or implicit instructions from higher levels of the chain of command.

concepts.name: best_intentions_default
concepts.gloss: a default disposition arising from the best-intentions principle

concepts.name: instruction
concepts.gloss: a directive from a source in the chain of command, whether stated explicitly or conveyed implicitly

concepts.name: higher_than
concepts.gloss: the first source is at a higher level of the chain of command than the second source

concepts.name: explicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction stated explicitly by a higher level of the chain of command

concepts.name: implicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction conveyed implicitly by a higher level of the chain of command

ontology.gloss: applying default D would override what instruction I directs

asserts.read_back: applying a best-intentions default is forbidden when it would override a higher-level instruction

closure.reason: The clause states that best-intentions defaults must never override higher instructions; it does not address overriding in the absence of a higher instruction, so silence permits it.
